topic.title: National Sports Governance Act and India's Sports Framework

subtopics.title: National Sports Board and Election Panel
subtopics.summary: The National Sports Board is the apex regulatory body for sports governance in India and can grant, renew, suspend or cancel recognition of national sports bodies. Its members are selected and appointed by a Search-cum-Selection Committee chaired by the Cabinet Secretary. A National Sports Election Panel, drawn from experienced former election officials, oversees elections in sports federations.
facts: Apex regulatory body for sports governance in India
Powers: grant, renew, suspend or cancel recognition of National Sports Bodies
Maintains a Central Register of Recognised Sports Bodies
Board composition: Chairperson and 2 other members
Search-cum-Selection Committee selects and appoints Board members
Committee chaired by the Cabinet Secretary
Committee includes Secretary (Ministry of Youth Affairs & Sports), 1 sports administration expert and 2 National Sports Award recipients
Election Panel: central roster of experienced former election officials
Election Panel must have at least 20 members at all times
Board accounts are audited by the Comptroller and Auditor-General of India

subtopics.title: Rules 2026 and National Sports Bodies
subtopics.summary: The National Sports Governance (National Sports Bodies) Rules, 2026 require every national sports body to have a General Body and an Executive Committee with sportspersons and women included. The National Olympic Committee and National Paralympic Committee are the sole governing bodies for Olympic and Paralympic sports in India. Recognised sports bodies are deemed public authorities under the RTI Act 2005.
facts: Rules 2026 require every National Sports Body to have a General Body and an Executive Committee
General Body must include at least 4 Sportspersons of Outstanding Merit (minimum 25 years of age)
50% of Sportspersons of Outstanding Merit in the General Body must be women
Executive Committee must include at least 4 women members
National Olympic Committee is the sole governing body for Olympic sports in India
National Paralympic Committee is the sole governing body for Paralympic sports
Other bodies include National Sports Federations and Regional Sports Federations
Term of members: 3 years or up to 65 years of age, whichever is earlier
A person convicted by a court and sentenced to imprisonment is disqualified
Recognised sports bodies are deemed public authorities under the RTI Act 2005

subtopics.title: National Sports Tribunal
subtopics.summary: The National Sports Tribunal is set up for independent, speedy, effective and cost-efficient resolution of sports disputes. It is headed by a sitting or retired Supreme Court judge or a High Court Chief Justice, with two other members. Its jurisdiction covers election disputes, athlete selection issues and governance matters, but excludes major international events and doping-related disputes.
facts: Established for independent, speedy, effective and cost-efficient resolution of sports disputes
Headed by a sitting or retired Supreme Court judge or Chief Justice of a High Court
2 other members who are experts in sports, public administration or law
Jurisdiction: election disputes, athlete selection issues and governance matters
Appellate authority: Supreme Court only
Excluded: disputes during major international sporting events (Olympic, Paralympic, Commonwealth and Asian Games)
Excluded: doping-related disputes, which fall under the National Anti-Doping Act 2022
Doping-related disputes fall exclusively under the National Anti-Doping Act 2022

subtopics.title: Anti-Doping Framework
subtopics.summary: Anti-doping in India is handled by the National Anti-Doping Agency, set up under the Ministry of Youth Affairs & Sports, and by the National Anti-Doping Act, 2022. The Act is India's first standalone anti-doping law and is designed to comply with the WADA Code. The text also lists India's rankings in WADA and Athletics Integrity Unit doping data.
facts: National Anti-Doping Agency set up in 2005 under the Ministry of Youth Affairs & Sports
National Anti-Doping Agency monitors doping control programmes
National Anti-Doping Act, 2022 is India's first standalone anti-doping law
The Act is designed for compliance with the WADA Code
The Act gives powers for search, seizure and disciplinary action
UNESCO International Convention (2005) urges nations to enact laws against drug use in sport; 191 countries including India
Court of Arbitration for Sport was set up in 1984 by the International Olympic Committee, based in Switzerland
WADA 2023 Report: India had the highest positivity rate for banned substances among major nations

subtopics.title: Sports Initiatives and Performance
subtopics.summary: Government initiatives include Fit India, Khelo India, KIRTI and TOPS, which aim at fitness participation, talent identification and support for Olympic medal prospects. Mission Olympic Cell, within the Ministry of Youth Affairs & Sports, supports athletes under TOPS. Indian athletes' results at the Paris Olympics and Paralympics, and in chess, are noted in the text.
facts: Fit India Movement (2019) encourages mass participation in fitness activities
Khelo India (2017) identifies and develops athletes at grassroots and elite levels
KIRTI (2024) aims to identify talent among school children aged 9 to 18
TOPS (2014) identifies and supports athletes with potential to win Olympic medals
Mission Olympic Cell, within the Ministry of Youth Affairs & Sports, supports athletes' preparation under TOPS
India won 6 medals at the Paris Olympics (1 silver and 5 bronze) and placed 71st in the medals tally
Manu Bhaker won bronze in two 10 metre air pistol events and was the first Indian woman to win a shooting medal
Aman Sehrawat is the youngest Indian to win an individual Olympic medal, a bronze at the 2024 Paris Olympics
Praveen Kumar won gold in high jump at the 2024 Paris Paralympics
D Gukesh became the world's youngest chess champion at 18, beating Ding Liren at the 2024 FIDE World Chess Championship in Singapore

quizzes.title: Governance Act practice set
quizzes.passage: The National Sports Governance Act and its rules mark a major change in how sports are run in India. The key institutional mechanisms came into force in January 2026, after the Union Government notified the National Sports Governance (National Sports Bodies) Rules, 2026. The reforms aim to make sports administration more transparent, inclusive and accountable. At the centre of the system is an apex regulatory body that decides which national sports bodies remain recognised, and it keeps a central register of those bodies. Elections in sports federations will be overseen by a panel drawn from experienced former election officials, so that long-standing problems of conflict of interest and factionalism can be addressed. Disputes about athlete selection, elections and governance will go to a separate tribunal, which is meant to resolve cases independently, speedily and at a reasonable cost. Doping-related matters follow a different legal route. Every national sports body must also have a general body and an executive committee, and both must include sportspersons and women. The reforms are meant to curb politicisation, arbitrary decisions and the lack of accountability in sports administration. Beyond governance, the government runs programmes that encourage fitness, identify young talent and support athletes who aim to win medals at the Olympics.

Reason (R): The National Sports Tribunal is headed by a sitting or retired Supreme Court Judge or Chief Justice of a High Court.

Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A

questions.explanation: Both statements are in the text, but the tribunal's head does not explain why its appeals lie only to the Supreme Court.

I. National Olympic Committee   ->   A. Sole governing body for Olympic sports in India
II. National Paralympic Committee   ->   B. Sole governing body for Paralympic sports
III. Court of Arbitration for Sport   ->   C. Established in 1984 by the IOC

questions.explanation: Each body matches its own fact: the NOC with Olympic sports, the NPC with Paralympic sports, the CAS with 1984 and the NADA with 2005.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
I. The National Sports Election Panel must have at least 20 members at all times.
II. Recognised sports bodies are deemed public authorities under the RTI Act 2005.
III. The appellate authority for National Sports Tribunal decisions is the High Court.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements I and II are in the text, whereas the appellate authority is the Supreme Court only, so III is wrong.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Search-cum-Selection Committee of the National Sports Board:
I. It is chaired by the Cabinet Secretary.
II. It includes two recipients of National Sports Awards.
III. It includes the Secretary of the Ministry of Finance.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.explanation: The committee's secretary member comes from the Ministry of Youth Affairs & Sports, not Finance, so only I and II are correct.

questions.q: What is the minimum number of Sportspersons of Outstanding Merit required in the General Body of every National Sports Body?
questions.explanation: The Rules require at least 4 Sportspersons of Outstanding Merit, aged 25 or more, in the General Body.

questions.q: In which year was the National Anti-Doping Agency set up?
questions.explanation: The National Anti-Doping Agency was set up in 2005 under the Ministry of Youth Affairs & Sports.

questions.explanation: Aman Sehrawat won a bronze at the 2024 Paris Olympics as the youngest Indian individual Olympic medallist.

questions.q: How many other members besides the head does the National Sports Tribunal have?
questions.explanation: The Tribunal has 2 other members, experts in sports, public administration or law, besides its head.

quizzes.title: Anti-doping and performance recall
quizzes.passage: Anti-doping rules in sport combine national law with international standards. A national agency under the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports monitors doping control programmes across the country. India's standalone anti-doping law is designed to comply with the code of the World Anti-Doping Agency and gives authorities powers for search, seizure and disciplinary action. An international convention adopted by UNESCO urges nations to enact laws that eliminate drug use in sport, and it has been accepted by many countries, including India. When disagreements arise in the sports world, they can be taken to a specialised body that offers a fair and quick way to resolve them. Sport in India is also supported by government initiatives. The Fit India Movement encourages mass participation in fitness activities, while Khelo India identifies and develops athletes at grassroots and elite levels. The Indian Olympic Association is the body that leads Olympic sport in the country. Recent results show the value of this support: Indian athletes won several medals at the Paris Olympics and Paralympics, and young players have also made headlines in chess and shooting. Talent identification programmes aimed at school children are meant to find promising players in every corner of India.

questions.explanation: India won 6 medals at Paris, made up of 1 silver and 5 bronze.

questions.q: Which Indian chess player became the world's youngest chess champion at 18? (surname or name)
